title: Requirement file
description: A .brain/requirements/<module>.yaml file: an array of requirement objects. Identifier patterns and the status lifecycle are frozen by CONVENTIONS.md; this schema is a transcription of that document, not an independent source of truth.

requirementId.description: CONVENTIONS.md §1. Never reused, renumbered or renamed once status reaches 'agreed'.

title.description: One line. What the requirement demands, not how it is built.

module.description: Must equal the MODULE segment of `id`, and must be a member of the project's declared module list.

status.description: CONVENTIONS.md §6. Forward-only, no skipped steps. 'agreed' and beyond require zero open ambiguities; 'verified' and beyond require at least one verified_by entry.

version.description: Incremented when the requirement's meaning changes. Incrementing resets status to 'draft' and appends the previous state to history.

history.description: Append-only log of superseded versions. The current version is NOT listed here.

source.description: Where this requirement came from: a BRD section reference, a call date, a client email. Not a guess.

rationale.description: Why the requirement exists. Business reason, not implementation reason.

acceptance.description: Machine-checkable acceptance criteria. A requirement with no criterion cannot be verified and must not exist.

ambiguities.description: Open questions for the client, each phrased as a question. Every entry listed here is OPEN; resolved ambiguities are removed, and the resolution is recorded in the acceptance criteria it produced. A non-empty list blocks the draft -> agreed transition.

depends_on.description: Requirements that must hold for this one to be meaningful. Must be acyclic.

verified_by.description: Test file paths, repository-relative, holding a @covers annotation for this requirement at its current version.

agreed.description: ISO 8601 date on which this version reached status 'agreed', or null if it never did.

superseded_by.description: The version number of this same requirement that replaced this entry. Supersession by a DIFFERENT requirement is recorded as a change record (CHG-NNNN), not here.

summary.description: What this version said, and why it changed.
